subject: Pricing follow-up & token economics — Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up & token economics — Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the ask from my side:

- Volumes: you mentioned expected monthly token consumption of ~10M–50M tokens (prompt + completion) initially, potentially growing to 200M+/mo in year 2. Please confirm if that still matches your model.
- Budget: you indicated an annual budget range of $50k–$200k for year 1.
- Target unit economics: you said Acme is targeting ~$40–$60 per 1M tokens as the target price to match your unit economics.

Attached is a light worksheet (acme_token_pricing_worksheet.xlsx) where I populated a few scenario rows with the numbers you gave. I also attached a short Redwood benchmarking summary (redwood_benchmark_summary.pdf) that shows representative $/1M token comparisons vs OpenAI and Anthropic across hosted and dedicated options. High level notes:

- OpenAI (latest completion/embedding tiers) tends to be ~ $90–$150+/1M tokens depending on model and payload mix.
- Anthropic publicly is similar range (~$80–$140+/1M) for the comparable models.
- Self-host / open-model hosts vary widely ($30–$120/1M) depending on quantization, latency, and SLA.
- Redwood Hosted (standard tiers) can be competitive for mid-volume customers; Dedicated/reserved capacity is the main way to reach the $30–$50/1M range you’re targeting with a commit.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the monthly token range that’s closest (10–50M vs 50–200M vs 200M+)?
2) Please share procurement contact (or confirm procurement@acme.com).
3) If you’re comfortable, I’ll draft a 90-day pilot proposal (committed baseline + overage) that models both Hosted and Dedicated price points so you can compare unit economics and SLA differences.

If that works I’ll follow up with a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a proposed pilot SOW + pricing tiers.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0134

Vanessa —

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications:

- Our near-term expected volume is ~30M tokens/mo (prompt + completion). We have a couple of high throughput flows that could drive us up to ~120M/mo within 9–12 months.
- Our current spend with OpenAI (for comparable feature set) is averaging ~$115 per 1M tokens after volume discounts.
- Target we'd want to see to justify switching is roughly $40–$60 per 1M tokens (your worksheet captured this well).

Procurement: procurement@acme.com is the right contact. Please loop in our legal contact (simon.larsen@acme.com) if you send contract language.

Happy to take a pilot — would like a 90-day committed baseline that demonstrates unit cost and latency/quality parity.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up & token economics — Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Alex —

Appreciate the quick response and the procurement contact. Based on the 30M/mo baseline + growth to 120M/mo profile, here are two pragmatic pricing options we typically present:

Option A — 90-day Pilot (Hosted + Commit Buffer)
- Baseline: 30M tokens/mo guaranteed for 90 days (prepay or invoice)
- Pilot unit price (hosted): $60 / 1M tokens for pilot baseline
- Overage: $75 / 1M tokens for any usage above baseline during pilot
- Goal: demonstrate parity and give you usage visibility.

Option B — 12-month Dedicated Reserved Capacity (Recommended for scale)
- Baseline: 30M tokens/mo reserved (can scale via burst policy)
- Committed price: $30 / 1M tokens (12-month commit)
- Burst / overage price: $40 / 1M tokens
- SLA backed and lower-latency profile for production flows.

Benchmark context (comparable public/commercial ranges):
- OpenAI (production completion endpoints): ~$90–$140 / 1M tokens depending on model and payload mix
- Anthropic: ~$80–$130 / 1M tokens
- Other managed open-model hosts: $45–$100 / 1M tokens (tradeoffs in latency and support)

Notes on unit economics: the key levers to hit your $40–$60/1M target are: (1) moving to a committed reserved capacity (or annual commit), (2) batching and KV-cache optimizations on your side to reduce prompt size, and (3) accepting quantized model variants where quality delta is acceptable.

I attached a short mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.docx) that lays out the pilot milestones (data/metrics we’ll monitor, success criteria, and procurement steps). If this looks good I can turn this into a formal SOW and pricing appendix for Simon to review.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll draft the MAP + SOW and share it with Simon (legal) and Procurement by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa will pick a discount tier we can offer for a first-year commit and I’ll include that in the SOW.
- Schedule a 30-min procurement/kickoff call this week to finalize PO timing.

Sound good?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
